s1.syndrome_frame: Cardiac dysfunction with possible infiltrative or obstructive process in the setting of a history of malignancy
salient_findings: Prolonged P-wave duration and abnormal P wave morphology on ECG
Diffuse medium masses in the right atrium on echocardiogram
key_facts: Patient is in their 70s
History of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
Treated with 8 courses of chemotherapy 4 years ago
No history of structural heart disease or hypertension
Blood pressure is 96/54 mm Hg
Heart rate is 56 bpm
Serum troponin I is 0.04 ng/mL
NT-proBNP is 3896.83 pg/mL
ECG shows prolonged P-wave duration and abnormal P wave morphology
Transthoracic echocardiogram reveals diffuse medium masses in the right atrium
PET-CT scan shows increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium and adjacent pericardium

shortlist.label: Secondary cardiac tumor
shortlist.why_kept: History of malignancy and evidence of increased metabolic activity on PET-CT scan

shortlist.why_kept: Presence of diffuse medium masses in the right atrium on echocardiogram

shortlist.why_kept: History of malignancy and evidence of cardiac dysfunction

raw.rationale: The patient's history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, the presence of diffuse medium masses in the right atrium on echocardiogram, and increased metabolic activity on PET-CT scan along the right atrial myocardium and adjacent pericardium are highly suggestive of cardiac involvement by lymphoma.

rejected.label: Secondary cardiac tumor
rejected.why: While possible, the direct involvement of the right atrium and the patient's history of lymphoma make cardiac lymphoma a more direct explanation.

rejected.label: Right atrial myxoma
rejected.why: Myxomas are benign tumors and would not explain the increased metabolic activity seen on PET-CT or the patient's history of lymphoma.

rejected.label: Lymphomatous pericarditis
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of lymphoma, the primary issue seems to be with the right atrium rather than the pericardium, making cardiac lymphoma a more fitting diagnosis.

rejected.label: Metastatic cardiac disease
rejected.why: The patient's history and the specific findings are more directly related to lymphoma involvement of the heart rather than metastasis from another primary cancer.
